rv.q: Christian Gerhaher is a compelling and wild-eyed Amfortas and Jakub Hrůša and the Royal Opera’s orchestra are superb G rail, wound, spear: some of the narrative trappings of Wagner’s final opera are immediately recognisable as symbolic.

Instead of dying in a blood-fest, Amfortas is meant to kneel in homage to Parsifal alongside Gurnemanz, who has also by this point disappeared. Arguably most shocking is the scene in which the Grail is revealed, and it turns out to be Amfortas’ unhealed wound, from which the community drinks his blood.
